This study introduces a free-breathing, motion-corrected 4D (3D plus respiration) T2-weighted turbo spin-echo (TSE) MRI sequence designed for whole-body imaging. The method integrates a respiratory bellows system with a retrospective motion adjustment algorithm to achieve 4D reconstruction from free-breathing data. The algorithm sorts k-space data into 4D volumes based on the phase of the breathing cycle, utilizing a novel motion adjustment strategy that incorporates a respiratory phase-dependent point spread function (PSD) to correct for slice profile distortions. Validation was conducted using phantom experiments and a comparative analysis against free-breathing 4D TSE MRI acquired via a respiratory trigger. Results demonstrated that the proposed technique successfully generated 4D images with superior spatial resolution and a higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared to the triggered approach. Furthermore, the method yielded a 10-fold reduction in scan time, requiring only 10% of the duration of the reference sequence.

This paper introduces a novel approach for synthesizing secure controllers for nonlinear, time-varying systems subject to both safety and control constraints. The method relies on an approximate control barrier function tailored to the system's safety constraints, known as an Input Limited Control Barrier Function (IL-CBF). This function is specifically designed to incorporate input constraints, distinguishing it from standard CBFs. Utilizing this function, the proposed controller guarantees that the system maintains safety while adhering to all imposed constraints.

This study introduces the concept of CF-approximation regions within a finite field extension $K$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, defined by a specific set of primes $P$. We demonstrate that for any abelian representation $\rho$ of the absolute Galois group $G_\mathbb{Q}$, there exists a finite extension $L$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that the collection of CF-approximation regions in $L$ (relative to the set of primes lying above $P$) constitutes a representation of $G_\mathbb{Q}$. Furthermore, we establish that the collection of CF-approximation regions in $K$ (defined by $P$) forms a representation of $G_{K}$ for any finite abelian extension $K/\mathbb{Q}$.

In the context of software engineering, structured tests are vital for validating that programs function correctly. These tests rely on permutations of pairs to evaluate specific properties, such as commutativity, associativity, and distributivity. However, generating these permutations manually is often error-prone and inefficient. To address this, we introduce a precise definition of paired-permutation generation based on the concept of a pairing function. We further present an algorithm that leverages this function to automatically produce the required permutations.

This study introduces a comprehensive dataset covering the United States cargo shipping sector, encompassing freight costs, shipping volumes, new vessel construction, used sales, and scrap values from 1966 to 2019. The data is organized into annual files, with each record containing information for a single year. This resource is designed to support research on maritime economics, the development of shipping cost models, and the analysis of sectoral trends.

We introduce a diverging triangulation, a triangulation of the fabric space associated with a triangulated surface that diverges toward the surface's vertices. We demonstrate that for any given triangulated surface, there exists a diverging triangulation of its corresponding fabric space.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) have become a dominant approach for addressing graph-based tasks, yet their reliance on complex internal structures often hinders human interpretability. To address this, we introduce a novel GNN architecture that incorporates learnable graph sparsification, enabling the model to identify and prioritize the most significant edges within a graph. Our method employs a differentiable edge selection mechanism that learns to construct sparse subgraphs, allowing for the identification of critical graph features. Empirical evaluations on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in classification accuracy while simultaneously generating more comprehensible graph representations.

Streaming matrix computations are essential for addressing large-scale machine learning challenges, with CountSketch serving as a foundational technique for these operations. This study investigates the robustness of CountSketch against adaptive inputs, specifically focusing on the scenario where an adversary constructs data to maximize the error of the algorithm. We demonstrate that, regardless of the adversary's strategy, CountSketch maintains a constant approximation ratio for the top-$k$ singular value decomposition (SVD). This holds true even when the adversary has complete knowledge of the CountSketch mechanism and can dynamically adjust the input matrix based on previous outputs. Our proof relies on a novel analysis of the adaptive adversary's limitations, revealing that their ability to create a significant discrepancy between the true and estimated singular values is inherently restricted.

In this part of the series, we demonstrate that for any compact scalar curvature manifold $(M,g)$, there exists a sequence of smooth metrics $(g_j)$ on $M$ such that $(M,g_j)$ converges to $(M,g)$ in the $C^{1,\alpha}$ topology, while each $(M,g_j)$ is either a trivial orbifold or admits a smooth metric of positive scalar curvature. This result, combined with Part I of the paper, establishes that any compact manifold admitting a smooth metric of positive scalar curvature can be approximated by such metrics on the same manifold. Furthermore, we prove that any compact manifold which is not simply connected and possesses a metric of positive scalar curvature also admits a metric of positive scalar curvature on some finite covering space. Finally, we show that any compact manifold with positive scalar curvature that is not simply connected must contain a minimal 2-sphere.

The entropy transported per unit time and per unit area by a two-dimensional vortex fluid is determined by the product of the vortex line density and the Nernst velocity. This transport entropy is inversely proportional to the vortex core's transverse dimension. Furthermore, it increases as the magnetic field strength rises, a phenomenon driven by the corresponding growth in vortex line density.

This paper introduces a novel framework for the real-time, collective management of learning-driven predictive systems. It addresses the challenge of dynamically optimizing a set of agents, where each agent's loss function is determined by a time-varying linear combination of losses from other agents. The proposed method achieves a regret bound of $\tilde{O}(d\sqrt{T})$, where $d$ represents the dimensionality of the decision space and $T$ is the total number of rounds. This result holds with high probability and improves upon existing techniques by a factor of $\sqrt{d}$.

This study introduces a novel hybrid framework that leverages BERT to generate stock price forecasts from textual data. By utilizing BERT to encode news articles and transform them into high-dimensional semantic representations, the model captures the intricate nuances of financial news. Furthermore, a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (CGGAN) is employed to forecast future prices based on these BERT-derived embeddings. The CGGAN is specifically chosen for its capacity to model complex, non-linear relationships within financial datasets. To validate the approach, the method is applied to the S&P 500 index, demonstrating that the proposed BERT and CGGAN combination outperforms traditional benchmark models.

This paper introduces a new shared envelope formalism designed to address the challenges of high-dimensional parameter spaces and complex likelihood functions encountered in Bayesian inference. By decomposing the joint posterior distribution into a product of a shared envelope and individual component envelopes, the method facilitates the use of efficient, high-dimensional sampling techniques to approximate the full posterior. We demonstrate the approach's effectiveness through simulations and by applying it to a real-world problem: inferring the masses of dark matter subhalos within the Milky Way.

We examine the production of two Higgs bosons in electron-positron collisions at the TeV scale, utilizing the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) framework. By analyzing the interference between tree-level and dimension-six loop-induced amplitudes, we identify the specific BSM operators that most significantly influence this process. We establish the necessary conditions for the process to occur as a resonant phenomenon and determine the optimal experimental configurations for maximizing the cross-section. Furthermore, we calculate the required integrated luminosity to achieve a 5$\sigma$ discovery significance.

We derive the field equations for a specific class of gravity theories by applying the principle of least action to a generalized Lagrangian, $L_g$, which depends on the metric tensor $g_{\mu
u}$ and an arbitrary function $f$ of the Ricci scalar $R$. This approach encompasses both the Einstein-Hilbert action and a broad spectrum of alternative gravitational models. We demonstrate that the resulting equations are mathematically equivalent to a set of differential constraints on $f$ alongside the standard Einstein field equations. Furthermore, we establish a one-to-one correspondence between these conditions and a specific family of Lagrangians defined as $L_g = f(R)g^{\mu
u}\partial_{\mu}\phi\partial_{
u}\phi + h(g_{\mu
u},\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a scalar field and $h$ is an arbitrary function of the metric and $\phi$.

We examine the collision of two localized shocks within a five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, utilizing the AdS/CFT correspondence to analyze the resulting hydrodynamic flow. By expanding the solution as a series of lateral gradients, we derive the hydrodynamic behavior near the shock front. This expansion proves effective for both the initial post-collision phase and the subsequent hydrodynamic evolution. Furthermore, we investigate the formation of a hydrodynamic jet and the generation of a shock wave, finding that the expansion remains valid for the entire process.

This study examines the asymmetric drag forces acting on a cylinder within a granular bed submerged in a fluid. We observe that the direction of motion significantly influences the magnitude of the total drag force. Specifically, when the cylinder moves parallel to the free fluid surface, the drag force is weaker than when it moves perpendicular to the surface. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this directional dependence arises from a disparity in the frictional resistance encountered at the cylinder's top and bottom surfaces.

The interplay between star formation and galactic outflows remains a critical yet unresolved issue in the evolution of disk galaxies. While observational data indicate that outflows can suppress star formation, the specific mechanisms driving this suppression remain unclear. This study presents spatially resolved observations of the nearby starbursting disk NGC 253, utilizing integral field spectroscopy from the MUSE instrument to map the distribution of ionized gas, stellar populations, and outflows. Our findings reveal that the outflow is highly structured, with its strength varying across the galaxy. We observe a distinct anti-correlation between the outflow's intensity and the specific star formation rate (sSFR), demonstrating that outflows are most vigorous in regions of lower sSFR. Furthermore, the outflow velocity is positively correlated with the sSFR, showing that stronger outflows occur in areas of intense star formation. These results suggest that galactic outflows are not merely a consequence of star formation but play an active, regulatory role in the formation process.

This study introduces a novel framework for Bayesian optimization that addresses the challenge of maximizing an unknown objective function while minimizing the total cost incurred by function evaluations. This approach is specifically designed for scenarios where the parameter space is vast, the function exhibits complex behavior, and evaluations are expensive. The proposed method, named BoGraph, constructs a probabilistic surrogate model that integrates an independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Gaussian process with a graph-structured prior distribution. This graph-based prior is derived from a directed acyclic graph (DAG) encoding the causal dependencies among parameters. By leveraging these structural relationships, BoGraph effectively reduces the variance of its predictive distributions, thereby enhancing the quality of optimization decisions. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that BoGraph achieves a regret bound of $O(d \log(T))$, where $d$ represents the intrinsic dimensionality of the parameter space and $T$ denotes the total number of evaluations. Empirical results indicate that BoGraph outperforms state-of-the-art Bayesian optimization techniques across various domains, including real-world applications.

We utilize the iEBE-VISHNU multiphase transport model to investigate the triangular flow ($v_3$) in Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 200$ GeV. Our analysis indicates that the initial spatial anisotropy ($\epsilon_3$) serves as the primary driver for $v_3$, with the initial state fluctuations playing a more significant role than those of the initial geometry. Furthermore, we observe that the initial state fluctuations are largely independent of the system's size, whereas the initial geometry anisotropies vary significantly across different collision systems. Consequently, the system's initial volume and the initial state fluctuations are identified as the key determinants of $v_3$ in both Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions.

The proliferation of RDF datasets across the Web of Data has created a pressing need for methods to assess their quality. While numerous quality frameworks exist, they often fall short in addressing the specific demands of large-scale RDF datasets. This paper introduces a novel architecture designed to evaluate extensive RDF datasets by integrating diverse quality dimensions. The proposed system operates in two distinct phases: first, it conducts a rapid, coarse-grained filtering stage to identify datasets of interest, and second, it executes a comprehensive, fine-grained evaluation on the selected subset. We implemented this structure within the OpenProvenance ecosystem and validated its efficacy through experiments on a corpus of 1,000 datasets, demonstrating significant performance improvements compared to running full evaluations on the entire collection.

This study introduces a novel, robust, and efficient method for estimating parameters in discretely monitored stochastic differential equations. The approach relies on a two-stage strategy: first, it employs a coarse grid to generate a highly effective initial estimate of the parameters, and subsequently, it refines this approximation using a second, more precise algorithm. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the proposed method achieves a convergence rate of $O(n^{-1/2} + n^{-1})$, where $n$ represents the frequency of observation. Furthermore, numerical experiments confirm that this algorithm is both computationally efficient and delivers superior performance compared to existing techniques.

We present the results of a detailed analysis of the chemical abundances in the circumnuclear regions of 11 Seyfert galaxies, utilizing optical spectra obtained with the Keck II telescope. Our study focuses on the ionization axis of each galaxy, examining both the active galactic nucleus (AGN) ionized gas and the surrounding interstellar medium (ISM). We identified a distinct population of shocked gas in the ISM of eight of the 11 targets, characterized by elevated [O I]/[O II] ratios and elevated [N II]/[O II] ratios. This shocked component is notably absent in the ionized gas of the AGN ionization axis, suggesting that the AGN's ionizing radiation suppresses shock formation in its immediate vicinity. The presence of shocks in the ISM is likely driven by the mechanical feedback from the AGN, which is consistent with the observed correlation between shocked gas fractions and the Eddington ratio. Furthermore, we find that the ionization state of the ISM is linked to the AGN's ionizing continuum shape, as indicated by the [O III]/[O II] ratio. Finally, our results demonstrate that the chemical composition of the shocked gas varies significantly among galaxies, with the [N O] ratio showing a strong correlation to the Eddington ratio.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is rapidly expanding, with billions of devices now connected to the internet. This IoT ecosystem relies heavily on event-driven architectures, where applications react to specific occurrences. However, existing testing methodologies for these systems are often inadequate, failing to address the unique challenges posed by event-driven designs. This paper introduces Event-Focused Testing (EFT), a new framework designed to generate test cases that specifically target event-driven IoT systems. EFT employs a hybrid strategy combining random generation with search algorithms to produce effective tests. It also incorporates a novel technique for creating realistic test data by leveraging the actual data structures of IoT devices. We evaluated EFT against state-of-the-art testing methods using two distinct IoT systems, demonstrating that EFT outperforms existing approaches in both fault detection rates and data quality.

The ATLAS collaboration has conducted comprehensive analyses of CP violation and rare decay processes in B mesons, utilizing approximately 30 fb$^{-1}$ of LHC data. These studies encompass CP violation in B$^0$ $\to$ J/$\psi$ K$^0$ and B$^0_s$ $\to$ J/$\psi$ $\phi$ decays, as well as CP violation and CP asymmetries in charmless three-body B meson decays. Furthermore, ATLAS has investigated rare B meson decays into two light mesons, two light leptons, and a photon plus a lepton-neutrino pair.

Traffic simulation is a cornerstone of intelligent transportation research, yet current methods often rely on hand-crafted rules that struggle to capture the full complexity of real-world driving. This paper introduces a new approach to traffic simulation that utilizes deep generative models to learn the underlying distribution of traffic scenes directly from data. Specifically, we propose a new framework called SceneGen, which employs a two-stage process: first, a scene parser extracts semantic elements from traffic images, and second, a scene generator reconstructs these elements to produce new, realistic traffic scenarios. To ensure fidelity, we developed a novel loss function that explicitly models the spatial relationships between objects. Experiments on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate that SceneGen surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods in both visual quality and the authenticity of learned traffic patterns.

This study examines the Ising model within a Cayley tree framework, focusing on the existence and uniqueness of weakly periodic Gibbs distributions. Specifically, it investigates scenarios where the pair potential adheres to a two-layer structure, demonstrating that such distributions exist uniquely under specified conditions.

This paper introduces a preconditioning strategy tailored for the linear systems arising from shape-preserving discretizations of second-order elliptic partial differential equations. The approach employs a block-diagonal preconditioner, where each block corresponds to a single element within the computational mesh. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method yields a bounded number of iterations for the associated Krylov subspace solver, ensuring this count remains independent of the mesh resolution.

This paper introduces the concept of collective ergodicity for sequences of measure-preserving transformations acting on a single ergodic system. We establish several characterizations of this property, including a dual formulation, and demonstrate that it remains valid under specific conditions when applied to the direct product of systems. Additionally, we investigate the case where the sequence consists of independent transformations.

We investigate the formation of dust particles in low-metallicity environments, specifically focusing on the conditions within molecular clouds. Our study examines how the initial metal abundance and the initial gas density influence the growth of dust grains. We find that the final dust-to-metal mass ratio is determined by the initial metal content, whereas the final dust-to-gas mass ratio is governed by the initial gas density. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the formation of dust particles in low-metallicity molecular clouds can generate a supernova explosion with a progenitor star possessing a pre-explosion mass of approximately 10 solar masses ($10 M_{\odot}$) and an initial metallicity of $Z = 0.0001$.

Although the majority of existing 3D object detection methods concentrate on identifying objects within a limited vicinity, this study introduces Far3Det, a novel framework designed to enhance detection capabilities in distant regions. We observe that current approaches often fail to recognize distant objects due to two primary factors: the absence of explicit modeling for distant object characteristics and the lack of utilization of contextual information from surrounding areas. To address these challenges, Far3Det incorporates a Distant Object Feature Module (DOFM) that leverages the distinct properties of distant objects, such as their small size and sparse point distribution. Furthermore, the model employs a Contextual Information Module (CIM) to integrate environmental cues, thereby improving recognition accuracy. Extensive experiments conducted on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate that Far3Det achieves a 2.5 percentage point increase in 3D detection performance compared to the baseline, marking a significant improvement in distant 3D detection capabilities.

Finding the ground state of a quantum system's Hamiltonian is a fundamental challenge in physics with wide-ranging applications in chemistry and materials science. This study introduces a novel quantum machine intelligence (QMI) framework designed to address this issue. The proposed method utilizes a variational neural network to map a set of single-particle orbitals onto a many-particle wave function, with network parameters optimized via a stochastic gradient descent algorithm. We demonstrate the efficacy of this QMI approach by applying it to several Hubbard model variants, successfully generating approximate ground states for systems where exact solutions remain elusive.

We introduce a novel framework for aligning non-rigid volumes to surfaces by integrating a data-driven biomechanical model. This approach leverages a statistical model of the human body to impose realistic physical constraints, ensuring that the resulting deformation adheres to biomechanical plausibility. Specifically, we employ a statistical shape and mechanical model of the human abdomen to guide the registration process. Our method utilizes a statistical mechanical model to define the potential energy of the tissue, treating the organ as a hyperelastic material. By minimizing the total energy—which combines this mechanical potential with a spatial alignment term—we derive a variational formulation solved via an alternating minimization strategy. This approach optimizes the deformation field and the transformation parameters separately. Experiments on both synthetic and real data demonstrate that this method outperforms existing techniques in registration accuracy while offering superior robustness to noise and outliers.

This paper investigates the conformal invariance properties of the energy-momentum tensor for spherical stationary spacetimes. It demonstrates that the tensor remains conformally invariant under a specific class of transformations defined by a conformal factor $\Omega = \Omega(r)$, where $r$ is a radial coordinate. Furthermore, it is shown that the resulting spacetimes are always asymptotically flat. Finally, the study derives the corresponding solutions for the Einstein field equations.

Unsupervised metric learning is a critical component of self-taught scene flow estimation, where the flow field itself serves as the primary metric for assessing scene similarity. However, current methods often suffer from suboptimal performance due to a heavy reliance on neighbor-based training strategies. This paper introduces a novel adversarial metric training framework designed to enhance flow estimation by eliminating dependence on neighbors. Specifically, we propose a dual-network architecture: a generator that constructs a flow field to generate metric pairs, and a discriminator tasked with distinguishing between real and generated pairs. By training these networks adversarially, the system learns a robust metric space without needing neighbor information. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on both the KITTI and Sintel benchmarks.

This study introduces a spiking random neural network (RNN) designed for categorizing images into ten classes, with the primary objective of minimizing energy consumption. The RNN relies on pre-trained weights and biases derived from a conventional convolutional neural network (CNN), which are mapped to the RNN's initial states. The network operates in two distinct phases: an initial training phase where the RNN is trained using the corresponding CNN-generated labels, followed by a categorization phase. The proposed RNN achieves a top-1 accuracy of 80.1% on the CIFAR-10 dataset while maintaining an average inference latency of 1.0 milliseconds. Furthermore, when deployed on a TSMC 28nm low-power CMOS technology node, the chip consumes an average of 1.1 mW.

This study examines the thermodynamic properties of a spin-aligned strange quark star subjected to a magnetic field and elevated temperatures. By employing the MIT bag model, we derive the equation of state for strange quark matter and analyze the influence of the magnetic field on the equation of state, thermodynamic variables, and the behavior of spin-aligned strange quark stars. Our findings indicate that the magnetic field significantly impacts the equation of state, thermodynamic properties, and the structural characteristics of these stars.

This paper introduces the concept of an "ideal pairing" within the category of cubic graphs and their coverings, utilizing it to establish a one-to-one correspondence between Hamiltonian circuits in a cubic graph and ideal pairings within its Cayley cover. Additionally, we define a novel structure known as an "edge-tint," which is demonstrated to be in bijective correspondence with ideal pairings for any cyclic covering of a cubic graph.

This paper investigates the prime factorization properties of polynomials with integer coefficients. It introduces the concept of a block arrangement for the roots of two polynomials and establishes a criterion demonstrating that if such arrangements exist for $f$ and $g$, then $f$ and $g$ cannot share an irreducible factor. Additionally, the authors present a novel generalization of Cohn's Theorem, which proves that if a polynomial $f$ possesses a block arrangement of its roots, then $f(x)$ is irreducible for every prime $x$.

The widespread adoption of containerized microservices has driven a surge in research focused on enhancing their security and dependability. A key technique in this field involves static analysis using system call rules to detect security flaws and verify correctness. However, manually creating these rules is labor-intensive and prone to errors, prompting the need for automated rule generation. This paper introduces Timeloops, a novel framework designed to learn system call rules automatically. Timeloops leverages the inherent modularity of microservices to construct a modular rule system, employing a bottom-up approach to synthesize rule fragments from individual code blocks and combine them into comprehensive rules. Furthermore, Timeloops incorporates a rule refinement mechanism to ensure the generated rules are both precise and exhaustive. Experimental results indicate that Timeloops surpasses existing methods in rule coverage and outperforms the state-of-the-art approach, RuleGen, by 10.5% in rule learning efficiency.

We examine the stability of the dark matter (DM) candidate within a pseudo-Goldstone dark matter framework applied to the $B-L$ augmented Standard Model, where the $B-L$ symmetry is spontaneously broken at the TeV scale. In this model, the scalar potential is shaped by the interplay between the $B-L$ scalar field and the Higgs doublet, while the pseudo-Goldstone boson (PGB) acquires interactions with Standard Model particles through mixing with the $B-L$ scalar. We demonstrate that the PGB can serve as viable dark matter by establishing the allowed parameter space that satisfies both cosmological observations and direct detection limits. Furthermore, we analyze the potential for the LHC to probe this scenario via the production of the $B-L$ scalar, which decays into pairs of PGB dark matter.

This work addresses the problem of optimal filtering for a system involving multiple targets and sensors, where the birth process of new targets is modeled using a lattice approach. Specifically, the probability density of a target's birth state is defined as a product of independent components, with each component relying solely on a single lattice coordinate. By integrating this lattice-based birth model with the Probability Hypothesis Density (PHD) recursion, the authors derive a corresponding lattice-based Cardiac (CL) density that retains the same functional form as the initial prior. Furthermore, the paper presents a Progressive Multiple Birth (PMBM) filter that offers an exact solution for the first and second statistical moments of the target population. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PMBM filter achieves a lower Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) compared to the standard Progressive Near Nearest Neighbors (PNNA) filter.

This study investigates the null controllability of a species dynamics model featuring internal degeneracy. Specifically, we examine a stationary population density equation governed by a weighted porous medium type, where the weight function exhibits degeneracy within a specific internal domain. Our findings demonstrate that the solution to this partial differential equation is controllable within a finite timeframe when the control mechanism operates internally.

This study introduces a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach designed to improve decision-making in soccer matches, specifically focusing on penalty shootouts. The methodology employs a multi-agent framework where each team is represented by a single agent, utilizing a centralized training scheme with decentralized execution (CTDE) to facilitate effective collaboration. To validate the model, we conducted experiments on a realistic penalty shootout simulation, demonstrating that the proposed DRL system significantly outperforms traditional heuristic strategies.

This study introduces a time-domain expanded source waveform inversion (ES-WI) method designed to simultaneously recover a subsurface's velocity structure and anisotropic elastic parameters. By applying the adjoint-state technique, this approach formulates an inversion framework for time-domain anisotropic elasticity that targets both velocity and elastic constants. To enhance computational efficiency, the method incorporates a time-domain expanded source operator, which allows the solution of numerous forward problems to be achieved using a single forward pass. Furthermore, the inclusion of anisotropic elasticity parameters ensures higher reconstruction fidelity for complex geological structures. Validation through both synthetic and field data demonstrates that this ES-WI method effectively recovers velocity and elastic parameters with high accuracy.

The optical anisotropy of a system is typically established by the spatial arrangement of its constituent atoms. In this study, we demonstrate that quantum compression can generate optical anisotropy even within a system of atoms arranged in a symmetric configuration. We examine a two-dimensional array of atoms, where the light-matter interaction is mediated by a single photon mode confined within a waveguide. We show that the system's steady state exhibits anisotropy when the input light is in a quantum compressed state, a phenomenon that persists regardless of the specific direction of the squeezing. Furthermore, we find that the degree of this induced anisotropy can be controlled by adjusting the level of quantum compression.

We present the analysis of AstroSat observations of the low-mass X-ray binary IGR J19294+1816, which captured the source during its 2019 outburst. The data reveal a prominent absorption feature at approximately 1.5 keV, interpreted as a cyclotron line that indicates a magnetic field strength of roughly $8 \times 10^{12}$ G. Additionally, a quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) was detected in the 0.5–1.0 Hz range, with a best-fit frequency of 0.62 Hz and a quality factor ($Q$) of 1.1. The spectral analysis suggests the source was in the supercritical state of the hard state, characterized by a power-law photon index of 1.6 and a Comptonization electron temperature of 25 keV. The observed spectral and timing properties are consistent with the behavior of similar neutron star X-ray pulsars during outbursts.

This study examines a two-dimensional voter model incorporating competition-colonization balance and chaos, utilizing a chaotic map to define the deterministic evolution of species' population densities. We observe that species elimination occurs when the colonization advantage is sufficiently high, whereas the system sustains species coexistence under moderate competition and colonization pressures. Furthermore, we demonstrate that chaotic dynamics facilitate the prolonged coexistence of multiple species.

Indonesian sundials, or *suryakala*, represent a significant historical legacy that has largely remained undocumented. This study aims to record sundials across Indonesia, with a specific focus on those bearing inscriptions. The research methodology involved a comprehensive literature review and a systematic field survey conducted between 2018 and 2020. The findings reveal that Indonesian sundials were primarily utilized for religious observance, particularly to determine prayer times. Furthermore, the study identifies that these instruments were crafted by Muslim communities, with the majority located in Java.

This study introduces a novel integrated data and power transmission protocol designed for device-to-device (D2D) communications, which leverages an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) to enhance the efficiency of both data transfer and power delivery. Within this framework, the IRS is configured to generate a constructive interference pattern at the data receiver while simultaneously creating a null at the power receiver. Consequently, the optimization problem is formulated to maximize the minimum of the data rate and power transfer rate, subject to the constraint that the data rate must exceed a predefined threshold. To address this challenge, a suboptimal solution is developed using a two-stage approach: first, the IRS phase shifts are optimized via a successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithm, followed by the determination of the optimal transmit power. Furthermore, the problem is also solved optimally by transforming it into a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) task and solving it through a branch-and-bound (B&B) algorithm. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that the proposed protocol significantly outperforms conventional data-only and power-only transmission schemes.

This study introduces a remote Single-Point Laser Doppler Vibrometry (LDV) setup designed to acquire two-dimensional structural responses. By integrating a scanning mirror, the system enables the measurement of structures across extensive areas from a distance, overcoming the limitations of traditional LDV methods, which are typically restricted to on-site operation and single-point data collection. The paper details the system's design, including the scanning mirror's control mechanism, and presents experimental findings that demonstrate the device's high precision and reliability. Furthermore, the study addresses the challenge of reconstructing full-field vibration data from one-dimensional scanning traces, proposing a novel algorithm that leverages the reciprocity of the wave equation to achieve this goal.

The Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) is a premier tool for characterizing nanoscale materials, yet its imaging and spectroscopic capabilities are frequently constrained by aberrations. While conventional correctors have successfully addressed spherical aberration, eliminating chromatic aberration remains a significant hurdle. This study investigates the potential of a programmable phase disk (PPD) to mitigate chromatic aberration by introducing a novel, non-standard operating mode. In this approach, the PPD is configured to generate a specific astigmatic phase shift, allowing the instrument to capture two distinct images at different focal planes. By combining these images into a single composite, the resulting reconstruction effectively eliminates chromatic aberration. Furthermore, this technique can be adapted to correct other types of aberrations, such as spherical aberration, by adjusting the PPD's phase profile accordingly.

In this work, we investigate the encoder representations of generative conversation models to determine if they retain adequate information regarding the latent assignment. We introduce a novel method for generating synthetic conversations based on the latent assignment and the prior distribution, which allows us to evaluate the mutual information between these representations and the assignment. Our findings indicate that while the posterior predictive distribution of generative conversation models is sufficiently complex to obscure the latent assignment, the encoder representations themselves retain a significant amount of information about it. Consequently, we propose a new class of generative conversation models that explicitly incorporates this information into the variational inference process. Experiments demonstrate that this approach yields improved performance on both the MultiWOZ and Switchboard datasets.

This study introduces a novel 3D LiDAR location estimation framework, termed AttDLNet, designed to address the challenges of urban navigation. The proposed network integrates a dual-branch architecture: the first branch employs a PointNet++ module to extract hierarchical features from raw point clouds, while the second branch utilizes a fully connected layer to process global embedding vectors. These two feature streams are subsequently merged via an attention mechanism to generate a comprehensive global representation. Finally, the integrated features are passed through a fully connected head to predict the vehicle's pose. Extensive experiments conducted on the KITTI benchmark demonstrate that AttDLNet achieves a 50% reduction in relative translation error compared to the baseline PointNet++ model, while also surpassing the state-of-the-art methods.

Streaming video transcoding is a computationally demanding process that necessitates significant processing power and memory, making it an ideal candidate for execution on cloud infrastructures. This study evaluates the performance of a transcoding system designed to leverage heterogeneous cloud resources, specifically targeting Amazon Web Services (AWS). The evaluation methodology involves comparing the system's behavior against a baseline implementation using Amazon EC2 instances, with performance metrics derived from extensive simulations conducted via the Java-based CloudSim toolkit.

The specific heat of a single-layer graphene sheet, doped with a finite density of electrons or holes, is derived within the grand canonical ensemble at finite temperature. The study reveals that the specific heat per unit area exhibits a universal dependence on temperature, governed solely by the doping level, and is mathematically equivalent to that of a free Fermi gas. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the thermal energy of the graphene sheet is significantly influenced by doping, leading to a reduction in thermal energy per unit area by a factor of approximately 1.5 compared to the undoped case. Consequently, the thermal energy per unit area of the doped sheet is roughly 67% of that observed in an undoped sheet.

Speech generation models are increasingly utilized in various applications, yet they often suffer from the generation of irrelevant or inappropriate content. To address this, we introduce MaskedSpeech, a novel framework that employs masking to condition speech generation on specific contexts. Our approach involves masking portions of the input text and training the model to reconstruct the masked segments using its own generated speech as the primary source. Experiments conducted on the VCTK corpus demonstrate that MaskedSpeech significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in reducing irrelevant content within generated speech.

This paper examines the spectral and orbital stability properties of solitary wave solutions for the Klein-Gordon equation coupled with an anharmonic oscillator. We establish the existence of solitary waves characterized by arbitrary amplitude and frequency, and we demonstrate that the mass-energy functional is differentiable with respect to these parameters. Furthermore, we derive asymptotic behaviors for the solitary wave profiles as amplitude or frequency approaches zero or infinity. Finally, we determine the linearized operator associated with these solitary waves and analyze its spectrum.

We investigate the stability of Q-balls carrying multiple U(1) charges within a theory featuring multiple scalar fields. Our findings indicate that a Q-ball with several charges is stable if its corresponding single-charge counterparts are stable. Furthermore, we examine the stability of multi-charged nuclei, which consist of Q-balls bound together by attractive forces. We demonstrate that such nuclei are stable when their individual single-charge Q-ball components are stable.

This study examines holographic dark energy within cyclical cosmology, specifically focusing on the transition from a decelerated to an accelerated expansion phase. We establish that this transition occurs when the cyclical period reaches a specific critical value, a condition that aligns with the standard $\Lambda$CDM model. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the transition is driven by the interplay between the cyclical period and the infrared cutoff. Our findings indicate that the duration of the contraction phase remains negligible compared to the expansion phase, a result consistent with cyclical cosmology theories.

This study examines the connection between the adjacency matrix of a directed graph and its scattering matrix. We derive a formula for the characteristic polynomial of the graph's adjacency matrix expressed in terms of the scattering matrix. Additionally, we establish a formula for the number of spanning trees in a directed graph by utilizing the permanent of its scattering matrix.

This paper establishes a non-commutative extension of Leopoldt's theorem applicable to $\mathbb{Q}$, covering both p-adic and classical scenarios. Specifically, we examine the p-adic independence of characters within the Galois group of Q, demonstrating that these characters are independent if and only if their associated p-adic Hodge-Tate weights are distinct. Additionally, we derive a non-commutative formulation of the classical theorem by proving that the Galois group of Q, when acting on characters with distinct p-adic Hodge-Tate weights, is torsion-free.

We examine the potential of Belle II to detect new physics via the production of axion-like particles (ALPs) in $B$ meson decays. We establish that ALPs can be identified through their displaced decay signatures, even when they evade detection in traditional searches due to small couplings. We present the projected sensitivity of Belle II for ALPs decaying into diphoton ($\gamma\gamma$) or dilepton ($\ell^+\ell^-$) pairs, where $\ell$ represents either an electron or a muon.

This study introduces a contextualized language framework designed to identify semantic shifts in terminology across different contexts. We define a contextual embedding for a specific term as the aggregation of its individual vector representations from various usages. By comparing these contextual embeddings with the term's standard static embedding, we detect discrepancies that signal semantic alteration. We evaluated this framework on a dataset of 1,000 terms, comprising 200 pairs of antonyms, 200 pairs of synonyms, and 600 single-concept terms. Results indicate that the framework successfully distinguishes antonym pairs from single-concept terms with 94% accuracy and separates them from synonym pairs with 90% accuracy. Furthermore, the model achieves 90% accuracy in correctly classifying terms as either single-concept or altered-concept.

The Kerr black hole (BH) solution in General Relativity allows for the extraction of rotational energy via the Penrose process and the Hawking mechanism. We propose that the spin of massive quasar-hosted BHs can be utilized to constrain ultralight bosons through the phenomenon of superradiance. Our analysis indicates that the spins of quasar BHs are generally too low to limit these particles using standard superradiance criteria. However, we identify a specific scenario where the spins of quasar BHs can be significantly amplified by the accretion of superradiant clouds formed around them. This amplification mechanism enables the spins of quasar BHs to serve as effective constraints on ultralight bosons.

Interkinetic nuclear migration (INM) is a fundamental cellular movement observed in the developing retinas of vertebrates, characterized by nuclei oscillating along the apical-basal axis within a single cell. Although the molecular mechanisms driving INM are well-established, the specific cellular processes that govern this movement remain largely unknown. By utilizing high-resolution 3D imaging of INM in the developing zebrafish retina, we demonstrate that nuclear motion follows a dispersive pattern. Our findings reveal that nuclei at the apical and basal retinal boundaries act as sources and sinks, respectively, creating concentration gradients that direct nuclear flow. Furthermore, we show that disrupting the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) impairs this dispersion, leading to a failure of INM. These results indicate that INM relies on a combination of cell-autonomous mechanisms and tissue-level physical forces.

Accurate Bayer pattern interpolation relies heavily on precise source segmentation, a task that is often difficult due to the inherent ambiguity of color image reconstruction. This paper introduces a novel approach to Bayer demosaicing that leverages the known color image interpolation kernel to derive a corresponding color image restoration framework. Within this model, the interpolation problem is defined as a convex optimization task, where the interpolation kernel serves as the constraint. By establishing a mathematical equivalence between this interpolation model and a specific class of variational regularization problems, the authors derive an interpolation algorithm that is both computationally efficient and robust. Furthermore, the methodology is extended to compressive video interpolation, where it demonstrates significant performance improvements over existing techniques.

We examine the behavior of incompressible polar active liquids containing frozen disorder across dimensions $d>2$. By applying the first-order hydrodynamic theory of active matter alongside a renormalization group approach, we identify a stable fixed point characterized by a non-zero fixed value of fixed polarity. This fixed point indicates that active matter with frozen disorder exhibits a distinct hydrodynamic state compared to systems lacking such disorder. Specifically, we demonstrate that the fixed polarity generates a long-range hydrodynamic interaction, which drives a divergence in the diffusion coefficient of active particles.

Scholarly cooperation networks are pivotal in advancing scientific progress, and comprehending their underlying mechanisms is essential for fostering further development. This study introduces a novel approach to analyze the structural evolution of these networks by integrating network dynamics with degree distribution analysis. Our findings reveal that the degree distribution follows a power law, indicating the presence of a "rich-club" phenomenon where highly connected nodes cluster together. Furthermore, we observed that the average clustering coefficient and average path length exhibit negative exponential growth relative to network size, while the small-world property remains stable. Crucially, our analysis demonstrates that the average degree of the network is directly proportional to its size, suggesting that the system's overall connectivity is intrinsically linked to its scale. These insights provide valuable theoretical foundations for understanding the formation and evolution mechanisms of scholarly cooperation networks.

The pseudogap phenomenon, characterized by a partial depletion of the electronic density of states (DOS) within a material's energy gap, is frequently observed in alloys and disordered systems. This study demonstrates that an artificial pseudogap can be generated in a three-dimensional disordered alloy by strategically aligning the Fermi level with an extrinsic van Hove singularity (vHS) located within the DOS. This singularity arises from the specific geometric arrangement of constituent atoms, which creates a unique electronic structure distinct from the intrinsic properties of the individual elements. By adjusting the atomic configuration, researchers can manipulate the position of this vHS relative to the Fermi level, thereby inducing a tunable pseudogap. This mechanism offers a novel approach to exploring pseudogap behavior in alloys and provides a new strategy for engineering the electronic structures of disordered systems.

This paper introduces a novel device designed to examine neutron behavior within the Aberdeen Tunnel facility. This apparatus consists of a high-intensity proton beamline, a target assembly, and a surrounding detector system. The proton beam, generated by the 100 MeV cyclotron at the University of Aberdeen, strikes a target to produce neutrons via spallation. The detector system comprises a scintillator array and a muon detector, both positioned within the tunnel. The design and operational principles of this device are detailed, alongside experimental results demonstrating the neutron flux distribution.

This paper investigates a nonlocal biharmonic Choquard equation featuring a linear potential, exponential growth at the critical threshold, and a nonlinear term that is positive. By applying variational techniques and a linking framework, we establish the existence of a positive, standardized solution.

The TESS-Keck Survey (TKS) aims to identify and characterize the nearest, most massive exoplanets orbiting bright stars, thereby enabling detailed studies of their interiors, atmospheres, and potential habitability. This initiative leverages the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) to detect transiting exoplanets and utilizes the Keck telescopes to measure the host stars' radial velocities. To achieve these goals, the survey prioritizes targets with high transit signal-to-noise ratios, which are selected based on the TESS photometric precision and the stellar radius. This paper outlines the specific objectives of the TKS and details the methodology for choosing these primary targets.

This study introduces an automated system for extracting data from Indonesian identity cards (KTP) using a hybrid approach that combines Optical Character Recognition (Tesseract) with Natural Language Processing (NLP). The system leverages Tesseract to capture raw text from the document, which is subsequently processed by NLP techniques to extract specific data fields. The proposed method was evaluated on a dataset of 100 Indonesian KTP images, achieving an overall accuracy of 90%.

We present a novel application of the path integral method to analyze the quantum harmonic oscillator under constant acceleration. By employing a discrete time-slicing scheme, we derive the propagator via a Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm. Furthermore, we calculate the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the system's Hamiltonian using the spectral representation technique.

The study examines the impact of the YORP effect on the spin rates of asteroids (10115) 1992 SK, (1685) Toro, and (1620) Geographos. Utilizing the YORP formula derived by Vokrouhlický (1998), we calculate the YORP coefficient ($\beta$) for each body. Our results indicate that $\beta$ values for (1620) Geographos and (1685) Toro are approximately $10^4$ times greater than the critical threshold ($\beta_c$) required for rotation-induced fission, suggesting these two asteroids have likely already split apart. Conversely, (10115) 1992 SK exhibits a $\beta$ value roughly $10^2$ times larger than $\beta_c$, implying it is approaching a state where it will eventually disintegrate.

This study examines the political discourse within Instagram's networked structure, analyzing how political accounts interact with one another. By aggregating data from 100,000 political Instagram profiles, we constructed a directed network to investigate its topological properties and the dynamics of information dissemination. Our analysis reveals that the network exhibits a scale-free structure characterized by a distinct community organization. Furthermore, we identified a core group of highly influential political accounts that drive content propagation across the platform. Finally, we developed a novel metric to evaluate the level of political polarization within the network.

A subset $X$ within a metric space $(Z,d)$ is termed Roelcke precompact if every family of $Z$'s non-expansive mappings possesses a finite-dimensional net that is $\epsilon$-dense for any $\epsilon > 0$. This study demonstrates that the collection of homeomorphisms of a compact, simply connected Riemann surface which act as sense-preserving on the boundary fails to be Roelcke precompact.

This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of various stellar parameter estimation methods for M-dwarfs, utilizing a dataset of 100 field stars observed by the M-dwarf Ultraviolet Spectroscopic Collection (MUSC). We compiled a catalog of 100 M-dwarf targets from MUSC, leveraging Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) astrometry and effective temperature ($T_{\rm eff}$) values derived from spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting. We then assessed the performance of different $T_{\rm eff}$ determination techniques, including the MILES spectral template matching, the MIST stellar evolution models, and the MILES+MIST combined approach. Additionally, we compared the reliability of surface gravity ($\log g$) and metallicity ($[Fe/H]$) estimates provided by the MILES and MIST templates. Our analysis indicates that the MILES+MIST combination yields the most accurate $T_{\rm eff}$ results, with a median absolute error of 100 K. For $\log g$ and $[Fe/H]$, the MILES template offers superior precision, achieving median absolute errors of 0.14 dex and 0.11 dex, respectively. Finally, we applied these refined parameters to derive the masses and radii for the MUSC field stars.

We introduce a dual metastructure comprising a metallic strip and a dielectric rod, designed to support line waves guided along the strip. This configuration enables the creation of a waveguide featuring a dual-unit-cell metastructure, which exhibits a negative effective refractive index. Consequently, this meta-waveguide demonstrates negative refraction and the ability to confine electromagnetic energy within subwavelength dimensions.

This study examines the computational complexity of evaluating conjunctive queries (CQs) over finite structures, with a specific focus on query classes that prohibit self-loops. We establish that the complexity of query evaluation varies between logarithmic and polynomial space, contingent upon the query's arity. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the complexity of evaluating acyclic queries is precisely P-complete.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm designed to convert regular functions operating on infinite sequences into executable code. This procedure functions as a bridge between theoretical computer science and practical engineering, enabling the realization of digital systems that integrate both finite and infinite computational components.

The branching ratio for the $B \to K^{*0} \overline{K}^{*0}$ decay remains undetermined due to the scarcity of experimental data. This study examines the magnitude of the branching ratio for the $B \to K^{*0} \overline{K}^{*0}$ process by analyzing the related $B_{(s)} \to K^{*0} \overline{K}^{*0}$ decays. The analysis indicates that the branching ratio for the $B \to K^{*0} \overline{K}^{*0}$ channel is approximately $10^{-7}$, a value that is too small to be detected in current experiments.

While the majority of bacteria and other microorganisms function as pushers, a minority known as pullers propel themselves by drawing fluid toward their rear. This disparity in propulsion mechanisms drives the formation of dynamic clusters, which are essential for the self-organization of active matter systems. Despite their significance, the ability of pullers to remain hidden within a sea of pushers poses a challenge for detection. This study demonstrates that a convolutional neural network can accurately identify these elusive pullers by analyzing the motion patterns of mixed populations, even when the pullers constitute a small fraction. Furthermore, the authors establish a theoretical framework linking the detectability of pullers to the statistical properties of the overall mixture.

Average absolute deviation from the median (AADM) serves as a robust measure of variability that is frequently preferred over standard deviation. However, naive estimators of AADM derived from sample data exhibit bias, particularly in small samples. This study introduces a bias-corrected estimator for AADM that leverages the known distribution of sample medians to eliminate this bias. The resulting method demonstrates superior performance compared to existing bias-corrected estimators, especially when dealing with limited sample sizes.

This paper introduces a second-order numerical approach for computing attainable sets within the context of stochastic differential games. The method relies on a novel numerical scheme designed to resolve a specific variational Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation, which emerges as the core component of a generalized Bellman-Isaacs principle applicable to a broad class of differential games. This principle extends the classical framework by incorporating a term that accounts for the second-order derivatives of the value function with respect to the state variables, thereby capturing additional dynamics neglected in first-order formulations. Numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the method's efficacy and validate its performance.

We introduce a cyclic activation mechanism designed to enhance the local functional representation capabilities of convolutional neural networks. This approach involves cyclically activating specific neurons within a single convolutional filter to generate distinct functional representations across different image regions. Unlike existing methods that rely on explicit supervision or external modules, our technique is entirely self-supervised and requires no additional training. Furthermore, it is cyclically modulated, which allows the network to adapt to diverse datasets without retraining. Experiments demonstrate that this method significantly boosts the performance of various deep learning models on multiple tasks, including image classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection.

Humans categorize objects into animate and inanimate groups, a distinction supported by a dedicated region in the ventral temporal cortex known as the animacy arrangement area (AAA). This region exhibits a unique functional organization where the left side processes faces and the right side processes bodies, creating a functional mirror image of the anatomical layout of the visual ventral stream. While the precise mechanisms driving this arrangement remain unclear, we hypothesize that it arises from the distinct spatial distributions of visual features associated with faces versus bodies. To test this, we employed a deep neural network trained on ImageNet and extracted feature maps from its hierarchy. Our analysis revealed that the network's visual ventral stream similarly organizes into a functional mirror image of the anatomical ventral stream, driven by the specific visual feature profiles of faces and bodies. Consequently, we propose that the animacy arrangement in the human brain is established through the distinct visual feature distributions characteristic of faces and bodies.

We establish the efficient equidistribution of Hecke-Maass newforms associated with the full modular group on the Riemann surface $\Gamma\backslash SL(2,\mathbb{R})/\{1,-1\}$, specifically demonstrating that their distribution approaches the unique ergodic limit at an optimal rate. This result is derived from an enhanced bound on the error term in the explicit formula connecting Hecke-Weber $L$-functions to the spectrum of $\Gamma\backslash SL(2,\mathbb{R})/\{1,-1\}$, which is subsequently employed to prove the Landau-Siegel zero conjecture for $\Gamma\backslash SL(2,\mathbb{R})/\{1,-1\}$, thereby confirming the non-existence of such zeros.

This paper introduces a novel relational quantum Hoare framework designed to verify anticipations within programs featuring quantum operations. Anticipation involves predicting future computation results and storing them for later use, a technique that anticipations can significantly enhance performance. While existing relational quantum logics have been developed to validate quantum programs, they currently lack the capacity to handle anticipations. To address this gap, we introduce a set of anticipative rules grounded in a newly defined anticipative quantum pre-post condition. Furthermore, we establish the framework's soundness and demonstrate that it can be extended to support both interference and exception handling.

This study examines the influence of super-spreader events on the course of an epidemic, utilizing a stochastic extension of the classic SIR model. By analyzing the stochastic SIR model, we derive the probability distribution for the total number of infections, accounting for the possibility that a super-spreader event occurs with a specific probability. Our findings indicate that these events significantly affect the epidemic trajectory, leading to a higher likelihood of total population infection compared to the standard SIR dynamics. Furthermore, we observe that the stochastic SIR model yields a lower expected number of infections than the deterministic SIR model, a discrepancy that intensifies with the frequency of super-spreader occurrences. Finally, we demonstrate that the distribution of total infections follows a negative binomial pattern when the occurrence of super-spreaders adheres to a Poisson distribution.

This paper investigates the properties of codiskcyclic operators and codiskcyclic operator collections within the context of Banach spaces. It establishes connections between codiskcyclicity and properties such as hypercyclicity, chaos, and the existence of an adjoint hypercyclic companion. Furthermore, it demonstrates that if a Banach space admits a codiskcyclic operator tuple, the associated Lie algebra generated by that tuple is necessarily chaotic. Finally, the work presents several results concerning the relationship between codiskcyclicity and the existence of a common dense orbit.

Solar vector magnetic field observations are essential for comprehending the Sun's magnetic evolution and its influence on space weather. However, the process of deriving these fields from raw data introduces various biases that can distort our understanding of solar magnetism. This study reviews the primary sources of such biases, including instrumental effects, data processing algorithms, and inherent limitations of the measurement techniques themselves. Furthermore, it outlines strategies to identify and mitigate these biases, with a specific focus on the impact of noise and the phenomenon of "noise-induced shrinkage." Finally, this paper presents a new method for quantifying shrinkage bias, demonstrating its application to data from the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) on the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO).

We present new measurements of the linear dimensions for 13 young stellar associations (ages < 100 Myr) in nearby galaxies, utilizing Gaia DR2 data to determine distances and proper motions. Our analysis reveals that these associations exhibit a wide range of sizes, with median diameters of 100 pc and a median dispersion of 40 pc. We also find that the median velocity dispersion is 1.2 km/s, with a median dispersion of 0.5 km/s.
